Entering via the leg nerves are 394 chordotonal neurons, 78 hair plates and 9 campaniform sensilla. Version 1, "tonic encoding" (firing by joint angle): the chordotonal neurons fire constantly at a mean of 8 Hz, pushing the network into runaway (237–274 active motor neurons); the original right hind leg rhythm disappeared, and correct and mismatched mappings gave the same result. Version 2, "phasic encoding" (firing by direction only while a joint moves, 0 at rest): receptors fire only 1–6% of the time; at 16 Hz the correct mapping kept the rhythm in 3/3 (version 1: 0/3), but still only the right hind leg was rhythmic, with no inter-leg coordination; the mismatched mapping ran away in 1/3 and in 1/3 gained an extra right middle leg, with no consistent difference from the correct mapping; at 50 Hz it ran away again. Conclusion: phasic encoding no longer destroys the rhythm, but the feedback does not bring out a gait either. The body is fixed with no ground load and the other legs barely move — a clear limitation.

对齐检验：在前足网络上，稀疏版参数与作者完全相同，运动神经元发放率最大差 0.1: Alignment check: on the front-leg network, with parameters identical to the authors', the sparse version's motor neuron firing rates differ by at most 0.11–0.15 Hz. In the full ventral nerve cord the rhythm window is narrow: at I = 250 nothing moves, at I = 350 12 of 16 replicates oscillate (8–11.5 Hz), at I ≥ 400 most run away; MDN at both strengths runs away 16/16. The rhythm appears in the motor neurons of all 6 legs (right hind leg oscillates in 75% of replicates under the main condition), but the inter-leg phases are not a tripod gait: ipsilateral middle and hind legs are almost in phase, with only 1–6 samples per pair; the swing and stance modules of the same leg are in phase (+0.94). Driving the body, only the right hind leg swings steadily at 9–10 Hz (0.6–0.7 mm, about 60–70% of the CPG); the other legs swing ≤ 0.07 mm (body vibration); during runaway all 6 legs thrash about wildly with no rhythm. Conclusion: one more rhythmic leg than the front-leg network, but still no gait.

全脑里 MDN 要双侧 LC16 ≥ 100 Hz 才放电，单侧不行；LC16: In the whole brain, MDN fires only with bilateral LC16 ≥ 100 Hz, not unilateral; LC16 also strongly drives DNa01/DNa02, DNa13 and the forward command BDN2. Game results: relying on backing up alone (cut giant fibre + cut DNa) gives 100% hits in all 18 cells, even though every threat triggered backing up — the fly was walking forward until it detected the threat, backing up merely cancelled the forward motion, and rolling balls keep rolling. Dodging relies on LC16-driven steering (with steering only, hit rate 17–79% at slope 5); adding backing up on top of steering doesn't help in most cells and makes some worse. With LC16 disconnected, every rolling ball hits. It cannot steer while hopping in place, so keeping the giant fibre often makes it easier to hit. 24 threats per cell; differences within ±20 percentage points are unreliable. The page still defaults to the pre-declared slope of 0.5.

稍好但没有质变：标定强度下失控更少（1/16 对 3/16），更多腿出现节律，常: Slightly better but no qualitative change: fewer runaways at the calibrated strength (1/16 vs 3/16), more legs become rhythmic, and the two ipsilateral legs right middle and right hind often swing in near alternation (replicate 1 phase difference 164°); but it is still not a tripod gait, swing and stance of the same leg remain in phase, and the front left, front right and hind left legs barely move. Phasic proprioceptive feedback keeps the rhythm in replicates that don't run away, but gives no more rhythmic legs than open loop; the mismatched control once gained two extra legs and once ran away, so there is no consistent evidence that the feedback content matters. The giant fibre → TTMn conclusion is unchanged: with chemical synapses only, TTMn barely fires (0–1 Hz); after hand-adding an electrical synapse equivalent to 1,500 synapses it follows at 23/13 Hz (old data 30/25 Hz), and giant fibre stimulation makes the full ventral nerve cord run away in 12/12.
